As for villains Deadline has been my favorite story wise.  Often the villains feel they are the good guy but in his case he is well aware of what evil he is doing to accomplish his goal.  He does not because he hates people but to spare folks of the same fate his people did.   Story and play wise I'm a fan of Plague Rat.   He is essentially a cornered Rat and his fight feels like that.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Depends on context.  I tend to default to Scholar, because the rest of my friends usually focus on deck control, card advantage, and damage, leaving me to tank.  But I love the archetype of the wise old man who everyone underestimates.  I like the Argent Adept and his variants a lot, too, but my friends usually don't appreciate how long my turns take when I play him.  When I need to deal damage, Chrono-Ranger is my go-to.  I enjoy Termi-Nation Unity a lot, but I only play her when I'm not anticipating a really hard battle.

I always hope someone plays Team Leader Tachyon and one of the Legacies, but I'm not fond of playing them myself.  My wife almost always plays Parse (we don't have Fugue State yet), and I'm rarely unhappy about that, she's a great asset.

As for villains, I think my favorite is La Capitan.  She's an exciting but not horrendously hard villain to go up against, with a lot of variety in her deck (although Advanced Team La Capitan is no fun at all), and I love her theme and her story arc (what little we know about it), and the whimsy in her cards.

posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
I'm kind of like Chaosmancer in that I love basically everybody, but to touch on some of my own favorites:

So like I said I like Argent Adept because I'm a big fan of both playing and listening to music and thus of playing D&D bards, so a bard superhero is like basically the best thing ever. His deck is also an incredibly versatile and strategic support deck, which plays into my typical gaming style quite well. Also the fact that he's cute and I have a fondness for redheaded fellas doesn't hurt any either.

I also have a soft spot for kid superheroes who are enthusiastic about superheroing and think it's fun and exciting, and Unity, Idealist, and Thiago!Ra all fall adorably into that archetype. Also Unity and Idealist get to make robots with their minds (albeit in different ways) and Unity's deck involves fighting with a robot army, which is the best thing ever. Especially since "robot minion army" is often a villainous trait so it's nice to see a heroic take on it.

While I already liked playing Absolute Zero's deck for its complex & offbeat approaches to combat, I like AZ himself even better after his podcast. I like that he focuses on how music affects culture (though I'm more into folk music on that angle than R&B), and spends time thinking about ethics and humanity in general. Also I can relate in that he's sort of worked through his depression to end up on a sort of anti-nihilistic attitude I tend to share myself (life sucks, people suck, everything sucks, but that just means you should try to do what you can on a personal level to make it suck less).

With Setback I can relate to his bad luck and having everything go wrong all the time (though I admit I am much much much less positive about it), and I mean he's pretty much like a human puppy dog, you can't not like him. Legacy might seem to serve as the SotM world moral center, but I think Setback is probably the one who qualifies as nicest guy on a personal level.

Finally, I can relate to Parse's data analysis skills and social awkwardness, and her deck is pretty much the SotM equivalent to a Blue/White Control Deck in Magic which is my fave style in that game. Also I wish I had Parse's hair.

In pure playstyle I find myself leaning to play the Prime Wardens a lot because they're basically Shenanigans: The Team.

On the villain side, Baron Blade is one of my favorites. I love mad scientists, and he's pretty much the platonic ideal of the aristocratic mad scientist. I so can't wait to see the Luminary deck.

I guess technically Citizen Spring is a villain? But I love her, she's so sweet and adorable and has the world's most tragic backstory. Poor Citizen Spring. :(

I love how creepy and freaky Spite and Biomancer are (also Biomancer is another mad sciency type), which makes me kind of sad that Spite's deck is so not-fun to actually play.

Greazer is downright hilarious. "Rockabilly themed alien bounty hunter" falls under that category of things I never knew I needed until it was presented to me. Also I mean, he's kinda polite for a villain in a way; he pretty much just takes his bounty and leaves, nothing personal to the rest of you.

In terms of playstyle, I like both Akash of the Many Names and La Capitan, since they tend to be fun damage fests but still with lots of strategy involved.

posts.cooked:
bobbertoriley:

And sorry to be the playtester that says something with exclusive knowledge, but…Stuntman. Oh my god, I love Stuntman.

 

You know, it is amusing to me that I can't decide on which new hero deck I'm most looking forward to?

 

The best I can do is say I'm least excited for Lifeline, and that's mostly because everyone else is ranking in at 11's and 12's for "How excited am I" and he's only getting like an 8 on the list.

 

 

Now that we know the full story on Matriarch, it's kind of hard not to love the reformed Lillian. She was a teen with a bad attitude given immense power. She did horrible things. Then she served her time, and tried turning her life around. No one fully trusts her because she did such horrible things, but she doesn't want to be that person anymore, she wants to be better, and she's willing to go the distance to make it happen. How can I not love that?

 

Seeing Blade turn his mad science towards the other side. I can't wait! No other scientist in our roster is willing to build such potentially dangerous stuff, and we're fighting Aeon Men, so he can cut loose and it's going to be wonderful.

 

Akash'Thriya? Amazing story of the evolution of the spirit of the earth, combined with really interesting mechanics involving the environment deck and working slowly towards growing into a victory. That has got to be fun, plus I want to see what she's capable of.

 

Stuntman, just from the two cards we saw looks like he will constantly be interrupting other heroes to be doing things that lead to him being in the spotlight. That's going to be hilarious and awesome and I really hope he has at least one card for kill-stealing from another hero, just because that is going to make me bust up.

 

And down the list we go again.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
I have to list two for each.

Heoroes:

Expatriette.  My first hero was Adept, but I fell in love wben I first played Expat.  From her "I don't need powers to beat you" attitude to the craziness of Flak Jacket and Unload, and the challenge of playing her when you don't get what you want.  She has remained my favorite hero to play.  Also she is really fun to make variants for, since you can really change her style when you do.

Fanatic.  Love a character that selflessly charges into combat, determined to win or die trying.  Love the economics of Sacrosanct Martyr and of course, the brokenness of ZEALOUS OFFENSE.  Final Dive is my favorite card in the game.  I don't play her as much because games tend to lack challenge when she is around, but I love every second when I do break her out.

For villains:

Akash.  Love the idea of this big chaotic spirit of creation that decides to redecorate, only to find these tiny pests attempting to stop her.  I think about her everytime I work in the garden and anger the ants that insist on living there.

Kaargra Warfang.  Love a game where anything not broken is too weak, and she delivers.  I like the theme of the fight, and really enjoy how incredible any proper variant of Fanatic is in the colosseum.

posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked:
I'll join in! While all heroes are my favorite, i'll list a few a certainly get the most enjoyment in playing.

 

Mister Fixer

He's a hero that is highly adabtable. I certainly find him to be more resiliant than a lot of heroes, thanks to Pipe Wrench and Driving Mantis. Grease Gun allows a round of peace, even if it cost him a round of doing anything else. Jack Handle also deserves an honorable mention for his resiliance, as it makes him immune to self damaging effects. Dual Crowbars makes him insane when he has damage increases. He's also responsible for so many powerful combinations within the game. If had to pick a hero to face a random villain it'd be this guy.

 

Absolute Zero

One of my earliest favorites. Also a hero whose play style was heavily influenced by the community by repeated comments about how you need both modules in play. The only variant I feel a desire to play Null-point is Termi-Nation. Other than that, it mostly enters play when I don't have anything else to play or I use Modular Realignment after discarding one. I really like the style of burning the heck out of himself to deal roughly half the HP of the VIllain Character Card. He's lucky to even make it through the match still standing, double digits is even more of an oddity.

 

NightMist

I am also for loose with her HP, but I tend to like her up instead. She's also the one hero where I can say I like one variant of her over ther other. Dark Watch NightMist increased my enjoyment of her so much. I love being able to plan her next round and have very few disappointing surprises. 

 

The Argent Adept

Supporting everyone else with The Argent Adept is entertaining. What is even better is while I am helping everyone else I get myself in a position where I will steal the final hit to the villain. One of my fondest memories of playing him in the video game was against Progeny. We were in the last round clearly going to win and the Hero after me bragged that he'd be able to finish the match as The Argent cannot muster the 9 damage needed to win. Unfortunately for him, after my previous turn I was already planning how much damage I could get on my next turn, which was 2 points more than what I ended up needing. Afterwards I was told I was the best The Argent Adept player he had ever seen.

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
I love characters where you feel you're building up to an awesome mega-turn, and Tachyon and Unity do that for me.

Besides, they have the best flavour text (apart from possibly Sky), Tachyon's a super-smart scientist and Unity makes awesome robots with her mind and I am so down with that. Also I had the biggest grin when I found out Tachyon is gay and it isn't in any way a big deal, when so many queer characters in other stories have basically no personality traits except their non-straightness.

Tempest was the first hero I played so I have a soft spot for them, and they are just too adorable with the dog and the eel but awesome and powerful with all the lightning stuff too.

And AZ is always fun because I like having to make difficult decisions about payoff vs self-damage and seeing how far I can push that before he explodes. His personal growth speaks to my soul as well.

 

There are lots of SotM characters that I like as actual characters but don't enjoy playing as much. Bunker has power armour which is a cool thing, but playing him feels so focused around modes that aren't that much fun to be in for me. Time-travelling cowboy? Awesome! But Chrono somehow doesn't satisfy me with all the plinky damage (doesn't make sense when I love Tachyon, but there you go) and the bounty cards I'm continually forgetting I have out. And I love bards and Argent's backstory is super cool, but even though I worked hard to grok his deck I just find him more work than fun to play with all the hoop-jumping you need to do to make him really shine.

But generally it's hard to pick favourites because they all have different things that make them awesome.
